result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now treated as test code (mock resources). I didn't write a test for the new cases, so the new folder shapes are unverified. The existing scoping and convention tests in `codeanalyzer` pass.

The change is in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, lines 393–394. The two patterns used to require at least one letter, digit, `_`, `-` or space after `mock`. They are now `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`, so the rest of the folder name can be anything except a path separator. That covers a plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/` and non-ASCII names like `mock-größe/` or `mock模拟/`. Because the match stops at a separator, `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` are not caught.

I did not run the old folders (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) through the new patterns. By the regex they should still match. Backslash paths need no extra pattern, because `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already tries the path with `\` converted to `/`.
